title: Distributional Policy Regret When Latent Subject Distributions Are Seen through Few Readings
banked_reason: D0.5: the constant-factor all-integer frontier and a matching observable continuous-reading rule remain the named open obligation; meets_floor=false, achieved tier incremental.
gap_reasons: The proposal's deliverable is an all-integer explicit frontier and certified attaining continuous-reading rule, but this node remains to-prove and the core supplies only an unmatched lower/upper bracket plus an abstract modulus equivalence, explicitly failing the required p=floor(log(n)/3) comparison.

For the Stat headline rate claim, no finite evaluable r(n,p) or rule certified within universal constants of the full-tuple lower directions is currently exhibited; the polynomial certificate is an evaluable upper bound, not the promised frontier-attaining deliverable.
The delivered note does not determine the requested all-(n,p) minimax frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a fixed-p nonidentification limit, exact testing witnesses, a polynomial-score upper certificate, and a one-sided logarithmic lower phase; the math review passed these partial results. It did not evaluate the true continuous-tuple modulus uniformly in n and p or construct a matching observable rule at the logarithmic checkpoint. The original field-tier headline remains open, so the sound partial work was banked at the reviewer's incremental tier.
tldr: A balanced randomized experiment observes each subject's latent distribution through \(p\) continuous readings. For the strict affine-density subclass, the complete tuple reveals only the first \(p\) latent moments. Beyond the fixed-reading floor and full-tuple testing inequalities, the paper proves a logarithmic-reading lower phase: for \(p=\lfloor\kappa\log n\rfloor\), root-\(n\) regret fails for every \(0<\kappa<\kappa_*=0.382720155917995\ldots\). The constant-factor all-\((n,p)\) continuous-tuple frontier and a matching observable rule remain open.
gap: Existing work covers bounded-reading nonidentification, causal distribution-function targets, and Wasserstein regression with sparse empirical measures, while general functional-estimation theory reduces affine problems to a chi-square modulus; no source evaluates the specified all-rule continuous tuple treatment-choice experiment uniformly in \((n,p)\).
fill: The project derives the tuple-specific frontier, matches it by an observable finite computation, and proves a converse against every randomized rule under the same unrestricted mixing-law model.
